# Individual Income Tax Brackets — Federal, D.C., and Alabama through Iowa

Research cutoff: **August 18, 2026**. Thresholds below are for a **single filer** and apply to the state's taxable-income base unless noted otherwise. They are marginal brackets, not effective rates, and exclude local income taxes. A state is labeled 2025 where its tax agency has not published a final 2026 return schedule.

## Federal

The official 2026 single-filer schedule is:

| Federal taxable income | Marginal rate |
|---:|---:|
| $0–$12,400 | 10% |
| Over $12,400–$50,400 | 12% |
| Over $50,400–$105,700 | 22% |
| Over $105,700–$201,775 | 24% |
| Over $201,775–$256,225 | 32% |
| Over $256,225–$640,600 | 35% |
| Over $640,600 | 37% |

[IRS 2026 inflation adjustments](https://www.irs.gov/irb/2025-45_IRB), [IRS Publication 505 (2026)](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p505)

## District of Columbia

D.C.'s official 2026 schedule applies to D.C. taxable income:

| D.C. taxable income | Marginal rate |
|---:|---:|
| $0–$10,000 | 4% |
| Over $10,000–$40,000 | 6% |
| Over $40,000–$60,000 | 6.5% |
| Over $60,000–$250,000 | 8.5% |
| Over $250,000–$500,000 | 9.25% |
| Over $500,000–$1,000,000 | 9.75% |
| Over $1,000,000 | 10.75% |

[D.C. Office of Tax and Revenue 2026 D-40ES, tax-rate table](https://otr.cfo.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/otr/publication/attachments/2026_D40ES_Book_wLinks04012026.pdf)

## Alabama

Alabama's current single/head-of-family/married-filing-separately schedule is:

| Alabama taxable income | Marginal rate |
|---:|---:|
| First $500 | 2% |
| Next $2,500 ($501–$3,000) | 4% |
| Over $3,000 | 5% |

The schedule is current but not year-specific on the agency page. [Alabama Department of Revenue](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/faqs/what-is-alabamas-individual-income-tax-rate/)

## Alaska

**No personal state income tax in 2026**, so there are no individual brackets or taxable-income thresholds. [Alaska Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development](https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/dcra/officeofthestateassessor/alaskataxfacts.aspx)

## Arizona

**Flat 2.5% of Arizona taxable income at every income level and for every filing status; no brackets.** The rate applies for tax year 2023 and beyond. [Arizona Department of Revenue](https://azdor.gov/forms/individual)

## Arkansas — latest official schedule: 2025

Arkansas has not published a final 2026 individual return bracket schedule. Its latest official schedule applies to net taxable income and is not filing-status-specific:

| Arkansas net taxable income | Schedule rate | Subtraction in official formula |
|---:|---:|---:|
| $0–$5,599 | 0% | — |
| $5,600–$11,199 | 2% | $111.98 |
| $11,200–$15,999 | 3% | $223.97 |
| $16,000–$26,399 | 3.4% | $287.97 |
| $26,400–$94,700 | 3.9% | $419.96 |

From $94,701 through $97,800, the rate remains 3.9% while the subtraction phases down in $100 income bands; from $97,801 through $100,000, the published subtraction is $89.30. For $100,001 and over, tax is **$3,809 plus 3.9% of the excess over $100,000**. The state directs table users to its $100 income bands, which calculate tax at each band's midpoint. [Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration 2025 indexed brackets](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025_TaxBrackets.pdf)

## California — 2026 estimated-tax instructions use the 2025 schedule

California has not published a final 2026 return schedule. Its official 2026 estimated-tax instructions explicitly direct taxpayers to the 2025 schedule:

| California taxable income | Marginal rate |
|---:|---:|
| $0–$11,079 | 1% |
| Over $11,079–$26,264 | 2% |
| Over $26,264–$41,452 | 4% |
| Over $41,452–$57,542 | 6% |
| Over $57,542–$72,724 | 8% |
| Over $72,724–$371,479 | 9.3% |
| Over $371,479–$445,771 | 10.3% |
| Over $445,771–$742,953 | 11.3% |
| Over $742,953 | 12.3% |

California also imposes a **1% Behavioral Health Services Tax on taxable income over $1 million**, producing a 13.3% combined top marginal rate. [2026 Form 540-ES instructions](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2026/2026-540-es-instructions.html), [2025 tax-rate schedules](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2025/2025-540-tax-rate-schedules.pdf), [2025 Form 540 instructions](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2025/2025-540-instructions.html)

## Colorado

**Flat 4.4% of Colorado taxable income in 2026; no brackets.** [Colorado Department of Revenue 2026 Form DR 0104EP](https://tax.colorado.gov/sites/tax/files/documents/DR_0104EP_2026.pdf)

## Connecticut

Connecticut's official 2026 initial single-filer schedule is:

| Connecticut taxable income | Marginal rate |
|---:|---:|
| $0–$10,000 | 2% |
| Over $10,000–$50,000 | 4.5% |
| Over $50,000–$100,000 | 5.5% |
| Over $100,000–$200,000 | 6% |
| Over $200,000–$250,000 | 6.5% |
| Over $250,000–$500,000 | 6.9% |
| Over $500,000 | 6.99% |

This is the initial tax calculation. Connecticut separately applies a **2% phase-out add-back**, tax recapture, and credits that can alter final liability. [Connecticut Department of Revenue Services IP 2026(7), Table B](https://portal.ct.gov/-/media/drs/publications/pubsip/2026/ip-2026-7.pdf)

## Delaware

Delaware's official 2026 schedule applies to estimated taxable income and is not filing-status-specific:

| Delaware taxable income | Marginal rate |
|---:|---:|
| $0–$2,000 | 0% |
| Over $2,000–$5,000 | 2.2% |
| Over $5,000–$10,000 | 3.9% |
| Over $10,000–$20,000 | 4.8% |
| Over $20,000–$25,000 | 5.2% |
| Over $25,000–$60,000 | 5.55% |
| Over $60,000 | 6.6% |

[Delaware Division of Revenue 2026 PIT-EST instructions](https://revenuefiles.delaware.gov/2025/PITForms_Instructions/Instructions/PIT-EST_Instructions_2026-01.pdf)

## Florida

**No personal income tax in 2026**, so there are no individual brackets or taxable-income thresholds. [Florida Department of Revenue](https://floridarevenue.com/faq/Pages/FAQDetails.aspx?FAQID=1466)

## Georgia

**Flat 4.99% for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026; no brackets.** [Georgia Department of Revenue tax updates](https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/important-tax-updates), [2026 Employer's Tax Guide](https://dor.georgia.gov/document/document-document/2026-employers-tax-guide-updated-june-2026/download)

## Hawaii

| Hawaii taxable income | Marginal rate |

| Over $9,600–$14,400 | 3.2% |
| Over $14,400–$19,200 | 5.5% |
| Over $19,200–$24,000 | 6.4% |
| Over $24,000–$36,000 | 6.8% |
| Over $36,000–$48,000 | 7.2% |
| Over $48,000–$125,000 | 7.6% |
| Over $125,000–$175,000 | 7.9% |
| Over $175,000–$225,000 | 8.25% |
| Over $225,000–$275,000 | 9% |
| Over $275,000–$325,000 | 10% |
| Over $325,000 | 11% |

[Hawaii Department of Taxation rate tables](https://tax.hawaii.gov/forms/d_25table-on/)

## Idaho — latest official schedule: 2025

Idaho has not published a 2026 individual return rate schedule. Its latest official single-filer schedule is:

| Idaho taxable income | Marginal rate |
|---:|---:|
| $0–$4,811 | 0% |
| $4,812 and over | 5.3% |

[Idaho State Tax Commission individual income tax rate schedule](https://tax.idaho.gov/taxes/income-tax/individual-income/individual-income-tax-rate-schedule/)

## Illinois

**Flat 4.95% of Illinois net income in 2026; no brackets.** [Illinois Department of Revenue 2026 withholding tables](https://tax.illinois.gov/forms/withholding/currentyear/il-700-t-withholding-guide-tables.html), [Illinois income-tax rates](https://tax.illinois.gov/research/taxrates/income.html)

## Indiana

**Flat 2.95% of Indiana adjusted gross income in 2026; no state brackets.** County income taxes are separate and vary. [Indiana Department of Revenue](https://secure.in.gov/dor/resources/tax-rates-and-reports/rates-fees-and-penalties/)

## Iowa

**Flat 3.8% of all taxable individual income in 2026; no brackets.** [Iowa Department of Revenue 2026 rate announcement](https://revenue.iowa.gov/press-release/2025-10-21/idr-announces-2026-individual-income-tax-and-interest-rates)

# Federal and State Major Tax Rates — Federal through Iowa

Research cutoff: **August 18, 2026**. Values use tax year/calendar year 2026 where an agency has published them; otherwise the row explicitly identifies the latest available year. Rates are concise UI copy, not tax advice. “Local varies” means the display must not imply a single statewide combined rate. All links are to government sources unless explicitly noted.

## Federal

| Category | Display-ready value and treatment |
|---|---|
| Individual income (2026) | **10%, 12%, 22%, 24%, 32%, 35%, 37%**. For single filers, bracket starts are $0, $12,400, $50,400, $105,700, $201,775, $256,225, and $640,600; MFJ thresholds differ. [IRS 2026 inflation adjustments](https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/working-families-tax-cuts-individuals-and-workers) |
| Corporate income | **21%** of taxable income; a separate **15% corporate alternative minimum tax** can apply to certain large corporations. [IRS Publication 542](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p542) |
| Sales/use and property | **None at the federal level.** General sales/use and recurring real-property taxes are state/local taxes, not federal taxes. |
| Estate/inheritance (2026) | Federal estate/gift tax applies above the **$15,000,000 basic exclusion per decedent**; maximum statutory estate/gift rate is **40%**. No separate federal inheritance tax on beneficiaries. [IRS estate tax](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/estate-tax), [IRS 2026 adjustments](https://www.irs.gov/irb/2025-45_IRB) |
| Pension/retirement | Pension and taxable retirement-plan distributions generally enter ordinary income. **Up to 85% of Social Security benefits** can be taxable, depending on combined income and filing status. [IRS Publication 554](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p554) |
| Investment/capital gains (2026) | Most net long-term gains: **0%, 15%, or 20%**; 0% ceiling is $49,450 single/$98,900 MFJ and 15% ceiling is $545,500 single/$613,700 MFJ. Collectibles can reach 28% and unrecaptured §1250 gain 25%. **3.8% NIIT** may apply above $200,000 single/$250,000 MFJ MAGI. [IRS 2026 capital-gain thresholds](https://www.irs.gov/irb/2025-45_IRB), [IRS NIIT](https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc559) |
| Automobiles/heavy vehicles | No general federal auto sales/property tax. First retail sale of taxable heavy trucks, trailers, and tractors: **12%**; gas-guzzler tax varies by fuel economy; heavy-highway use tax applies at 55,000+ lb. [IRS Publication 510](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p510), [IRS trucking tax center](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/trucking-tax-center) |
| Fuel/environment | Gasoline **18.4¢/gal**; diesel/kerosene **24.4¢/gal**. 2026 petroleum Superfund tax **$0.18/barrel**; taxable chemicals/substances use separate schedules. [IRS Publication 510](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p510), [2026 Form 6627 instructions](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i6627) |
| Tobacco/alcohol/other special | Small cigarettes **$1.01/pack of 20**; general beer rate **$18/barrel**; general distilled-spirits rate **$13.50/proof gallon** (producer/importer reductions may apply). [TTB federal excise rates](https://www.ttb.gov/taxes/tax-audit/taxes-and-filing/tax-rates) |

## Alabama

| Category | Display-ready value and treatment |
|---|---|
| Individual income | **2%, 4%, 5%**; top rate begins above $3,000 taxable income single/$6,000 MFJ. [Alabama DOR individual income tax](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/tax-types/individual-income-tax/) |
| Corporate income | **6.5%** of Alabama taxable income. [Alabama DOR income-tax incentives](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/tax-incentives/income-tax-incentives/) |
| Sales/use | State general **4%**; groceries **2%** from Sept. 1, 2025; automobiles **2%**; qualifying manufacturing/farm machinery **1.5%**. **County/municipal add-ons vary.** [Alabama DOR state rates](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/sales-use/state-sales-use-tax-rates/) |
| Property | State ad valorem levy **6.5 mills**, plus **county, municipal, and school millages that vary locally**. Assessment ratios vary by class (for example, owner-occupied residential Class III is 10%). [Alabama DOR property tax](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/tax-types/property-ad-valorem-tax/) |
| Estate/inheritance | **None for current decedents; Alabama estate-tax filings are no longer required.** [Alabama DOR due dates](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/individual-corporate/due-dates/) |
| Pension/retirement | Social Security, federal/state/local government pensions, military retirement, and qualifying defined-benefit plan payments are exempt; taxable IRAs/other retirement income use ordinary rates up to 5%. [Alabama DOR exempt income](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/individual-corporate/income-exempt-from-alabama-income-taxation/) |
| Investment/capital gains | No preferential rate: taxable gains, dividends, and interest are ordinary income at **2%–5%** unless specifically exempt. [Alabama DOR reportable income](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/individual-corporate/income-to-be-reported-on-the-alabama-income-tax-return/) |
| Automobiles | Vehicle sales/use tax **2% state + local add-ons**; annual ad valorem tax and registration depend on vehicle value and locality. [Alabama DOR state sales/use rates](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/sales-use/state-sales-use-tax-rates/), [Alabama DOR property tax](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/tax-types/property-ad-valorem-tax/) |
| Fuel/environment | Gasoline **30¢/gal**; diesel **31¢/gal** from July 1, 2025; inspection and other product fees may also apply. [Alabama DOR motor-fuel rates](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/business-license/motor-fuels-tax-rates/) |
| Tobacco/other special | Cigarettes **67.5¢/pack of 20**; other tobacco rates vary by product. [Alabama DOR tobacco rates](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/business-license/tobacco-tax-rates/) |

## Alaska

| Category | Display-ready value and treatment |
|---|---|
| Individual income | **None.** Alaska does not impose an individual income tax; therefore pension, Social Security, dividends, and individual capital gains have no Alaska income tax. [Alaska DOR revenue sources book](https://dor.alaska.gov/docs/default-source/homepage-documents/revenue-sources-book---fall-2023.pdf) |
| Corporate income | Graduated **0%–9.4%** on Alaska taxable income. [Alaska Legislature, 2024 revenue sources](https://www.akleg.gov/basis/get_documents.asp?docid=2388&session=34) |
| Sales/use | **No statewide sales tax. Municipal sales taxes may apply and vary locally.** [Alaska Commerce sales-tax information](https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/dcra/OfficeoftheStateAssessor/AlaskaSalesTaxInformation.aspx) |
| Property | **No statewide real-property levy.** Municipalities and boroughs may levy property tax; substantial unincorporated areas have none. Rates vary by jurisdiction. [Alaska Commerce property tax](https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/dcra/LocalGovernmentResourceDesk/TaxationAssessment/PropertyTax) |
| Estate/inheritance | **None currently.** Alaska has no state estate or inheritance tax; federal estate tax may still apply. [Alaska DOR revenue sources book](https://dor.alaska.gov/docs/default-source/homepage-documents/revenue-sources-book---fall-2023.pdf) |
| Pension/retirement and investments | **No Alaska individual income tax**, so retirement distributions, Social Security, interest, dividends, and capital gains are not taxed at the state income-tax level. [Alaska DOR revenue sources book](https://dor.alaska.gov/docs/default-source/homepage-documents/revenue-sources-book---fall-2023.pdf) |
| Automobiles | No statewide vehicle sales tax; **local sales tax and municipal motor-vehicle registration tax may vary**. State title/registration fees still apply. [Alaska Commerce sales-tax information](https://www.commerce.alaska.gov/web/dcra/OfficeoftheStateAssessor/AlaskaSalesTaxInformation.aspx) |
| Fuel/environment | Highway gasoline/diesel **8¢/gal**; marine **5¢/gal**; aviation gasoline **4.7¢/gal**; jet **3.2¢/gal**. Local fuel taxes can apply. [Alaska DOR revenue sources book](https://dor.alaska.gov/docs/default-source/homepage-documents/revenue-sources-book---fall-2023.pdf) |
| Tobacco/alcohol/cannabis | Cigarettes **$2/pack**; other tobacco **75% of wholesale**. Alcohol: spirits **$12.80/gal**, wine **$2.50/gal**, beer **$1.07/gal**. Marijuana flower **$50/oz** at wholesale, with lower rates for immature/abnormal product. [Alaska Legislature tax overview](https://www.akleg.gov/basis/get_documents.asp?docid=3355&session=33) |

## Arizona

| Category | Display-ready value and treatment |
|---|---|
| Individual income | Flat **2.5%** for tax year 2023 onward. [Arizona DOR individual forms](https://azdor.gov/forms/individual) |
| Corporate income | **4.9%** of Arizona taxable income. [Arizona DOR corporate estimated-tax booklet](https://azdor.gov/sites/default/files/2023-12/FORMS_CORPORATE_2024_120_165ESBooklet.pdf) |
| Sales/use (TPT) | State retail transaction privilege tax **5.6%**; county and city rates **vary by location and activity**. TPT is legally imposed on the seller but commonly passed through. [Arizona DOR 2026 rate table](https://azdor.gov/sites/default/files/document/TPT_RATETABLE_07012026.pdf) |
| Property | No single statewide effective rate. County assessors determine value/class; the overall rate combines county, city, school, and special-district levies. [Arizona DOR property FAQ](https://azdor.gov/business/property-tax/property-tax-faqs) |
| Estate/inheritance | **None.** Estate tax ended for deaths after 2004; Arizona imposes no inheritance or gift tax. [Arizona DOR annual report](https://azdor.gov/sites/default/files/2023-03/REPORTS_ANNUAL_2015_ASSETS_fy15_annual_report.pdf) |
| Pension/retirement | Social Security and railroad retirement are exempt; U.S. uniformed-services retired pay is fully subtractable. Other pensions generally taxable; up to **$2,500** of qualifying federal/Arizona public pension may be subtracted. [Arizona DOR Form 140 instructions](https://azdor.gov/sites/default/files/document/FORMS_INDIVIDUAL_2025_140i.pdf), [Arizona DOR taxable-income guidance](https://azdor.gov/individuals/income-tax-filing-assistance/identifying-other-taxable-income) |
| Investment/capital gains | Generally taxed at 2.5%; **25% subtraction** for qualifying net long-term gain on assets acquired after Dec. 31, 2011 (effective state rate **1.875%** on that qualifying gain). [Arizona Form 140 instructions](https://azdor.gov/sites/default/files/document/FORMS_INDIVIDUAL_2025_140i.pdf) |
| Automobiles | Dealer/private purchases can owe state/local TPT or use tax. Annual VLT: assessed value starts at 60% of MSRP and declines 16.25% yearly; **$2.80 per $100 new / $2.89 used** assessed value. [Arizona DOT registration-fee guide](https://azdot.gov/sites/default/files/2019/08/AZ-registration-fees.pdf) |
| Fuel/environment | Gasoline and light-class diesel **18¢/gal**; use fuel for heavy vehicles generally **26¢/gal**. [Arizona DOR fuel-tax report](https://azdor.gov/sites/default/files/2023-03/REPORTS_EXPENDITURES_2003_fy03-preliminary-tax-expenditure-report.pdf) |
| Tobacco/cannabis | Cigarettes **$2/pack of 20**. Adult-use marijuana: **16% state excise tax + applicable TPT**. [Arizona DOR tobacco FAQ](https://azdor.gov/business/tobacco-luxury-tax/tobacco-luxury-tax-faqs), [Arizona DOR adult-use marijuana](https://azdor.gov/business/transaction-privilege-tax/adult-use-marijuana) |

## Arkansas

| Category | Display-ready value and treatment |
|---|---|
| Individual income (2025) | Graduated; top marginal rate **3.9%**. [Arkansas DFA 2025 instructions](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025_AR1000F_and_AR1000NR_Instructions.pdf) |
| Corporate income | Graduated **1%–4.3%**; 4.3% applies over $11,000 taxable income. [Arkansas DFA corporate instructions](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/CorporationIncomeTaxInstructions_2024.pdf) |
| Sales/use (2026) | State general **6.5%**; state grocery rate **0% from Jan. 1, 2026**; city/county taxes vary. [Arkansas DFA state rates](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/office/taxes/excise-tax-administration/sales-use-tax/sales-use-tax-rates/state-sales-use-tax-rates/), [local rate tables](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/office/taxes/excise-tax-administration/sales-use-tax/sales-use-tax-rates/city-and-county-sales-use-tax-rates/) |
| Property | Property is generally assessed at **20% of value**, then multiplied by **local millage**; no single statewide property-tax rate. [Arkansas DFA assessment guidance](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025-Guidelines-Report-Handout.pdf) |
| Estate/inheritance | **None.** Estate tax repealed for deaths from Jan. 1, 2005; no Arkansas inheritance or gift tax. [Arkansas DFA estate tax](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/605-EstateTax.pdf), [Arkansas estate instructions](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/AR321_2003.pdf) |
| Pension/retirement | Social Security/railroad benefits exempt. Qualifying pension/IRA income has up to a **$6,000 per-person exclusion**; military pension exempt. [Arkansas DFA pension guidance](https://dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/206-PensionsAnnuities.pdf), [Arkansas tax exemptions](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/SalesTaxExemptionsFY2025.pdf) |
| Investment/capital gains | **50% of net long-term capital gain is excluded**; with a 3.9% top rate, maximum effective rate on qualifying gain is **1.95%**. Other investment income uses ordinary rates. [Arkansas DFA 2025 PTE instructions](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/AR1100PET_Instructions_2025.pdf) |
| Automobiles | New/most taxable vehicle purchases **6.5% state + local tax**. Used vehicle purchase price $4,000 or less is exempt; $4,000–$9,999.99 uses **3.5% state**; local treatment/caps vary. [Arkansas DFA motor-vehicle FAQ](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/office/motor-vehicle/faqs-for-dsmv/) |
| Fuel/environment | Gasoline/gasohol **24.7¢/gal**; clear diesel **28.5¢/gal**; petroleum environmental fee **0.3¢/gal**. [Arkansas DFA motor-fuel rates](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/MotorFuelTaxRates.pdf) |
| Tobacco/alcohol/other | Cigarettes **$1.15/pack**; other tobacco **68% of manufacturer invoice price**. Mixed drinks: **10% + 4% additional** state taxes, on top of applicable sales tax. [Arkansas DFA miscellaneous taxes](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/office/taxes/excise-tax-administration/miscellaneous-tax/miscellaneous-tax-descriptions/), [state sales/use rates](https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/office/taxes/excise-tax-administration/sales-use-tax/sales-use-tax-rates/state-sales-use-tax-rates/) |

## California

| Category | Display-ready value and treatment |
|---|---|
| Individual income (2025) | **1%, 2%, 4%, 6%, 8%, 9.3%, 10.3%, 11.3%, 12.3%**, plus **1% Mental Health Services Tax** on taxable income over $1 million; maximum **13.3%**. [California FTB 2025 schedules](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2025/2025-540-tax-rate-schedules.pdf) |
| Corporate income | General C corporation **8.84%**; bank/financial corporation **10.84%**. [California FTB Form 593 instructions](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2025/2025-593-instructions.html) |
| Sales/use (2026) | Statewide base **7.25%**; district taxes add **0.10%–2.00% each** and combined rates vary by address. [CDTFA sales/use rates](https://cdtfa.ca.gov/taxes-and-fees/sales-use-tax-rates.htm/) |
| Property | Proposition 13 base levy generally **1% of assessed value + voter-approved debt**; assessed-value growth generally capped at 2% annually until change of ownership/new construction. Local effective bills vary. [California BOE property tax](https://www.boe.ca.gov/proptaxes/decline-in-value/) |
| Estate/inheritance | **None for current decedents.** California does not impose a separate inheritance tax; state estate tax is inoperative without the federal state-death-tax credit. [California Controller estate tax](https://www.sco.ca.gov/ardtax_estate_tax.html) |
| Pension/retirement | Social Security and railroad retirement are exempt; most private, public, and out-of-state pension/IRA distributions are taxable at ordinary rates. [California FTB Social Security](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/personal/income-types/social-security.html) |
| Investment/capital gains | **No preferential California rate**; gains are ordinary income, up to **13.3%** including the millionaires tax. [California FTB capital gains](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/personal/income-types/capital-gains-and-losses.html) |

| Category | Display-ready value and treatment |

[Iowa DOR 2026 rate](https://revenue.iowa.gov/press-release/2025-10-21/idr-announces-2026-individual-income-tax-and-interest-rates), [Iowa tax/fee rates](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/general/iowa-taxfee-descriptions-and-rates) |

[Iowa DOR sales/use guide](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/sales-use-excise-tax/sales-use-tax-guide), [Iowa sales-tax FAQ](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/frequently-asked-questions/sales-tax) |

Composite local rate combines county, city, school, and special levies per $1,000 taxable value; assessed value generally 100% of market before statewide rollbacks/limitations. [Iowa DOR tax/fee rates](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/general/iowa-taxfee-descriptions-and-rates) |
| Estate/inheritance | **None for deaths from Jan. 1, 2025.** Iowa estate tax repealed for deaths from Jan. 1, 2005; inheritance tax fully phased out for 2025 deaths onward. [Iowa DOR inheritance-tax introduction](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/inheritance-tax/introduction-iowa-inheritance-tax) |
| Pension/retirement | Social Security exempt. Eligible taxpayers age 55+, disabled, or qualifying survivors may exclude **100% of qualifying pension, IRA, annuity, and retirement-plan income**; military retirement also exempt. [Iowa DOR retirement guidance](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/individual-income-tax/retirement-income-tax-guidance), [2025 expanded instructions](https://revenue.iowa.gov/media/4435/download?inline=) |

[Iowa DOR individual provisions](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/individual-income-tax/individual-income-tax-provisions), [capital-gain deduction](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/individual-income-tax/iowa-capital-gain-deduction) |
| Automobiles | Vehicles subject to registration are exempt from sales tax but owe **$10 + 5% fee for new registration** on sale/lease price, including private sales; annual registration also varies by vehicle. [Iowa DOR tax/fee rates](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/general/iowa-taxfee-descriptions-and-rates) |

Hazardous-waste and household-hazardous-material fees are separate. [Iowa DOR 2026 fuel rates](https://revenue.iowa.gov/press-release/2026-01-27/iowa-fuel-tax-rate-change-effective-july-1-2026), [tax/fee descriptions](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/general/iowa-taxfee-descriptions-and-rates) |

Drug stamp: processed marijuana **$5/gram**. [Iowa DOR tax/fee rates](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/general/iowa-taxfee-descriptions-and-rates) |

## Data-use notes

- Preserve the year/effective-date label alongside every rate. Do not silently present a 2025 income-tax schedule as 2026.
- For property tax, sales-tax add-ons, county income tax, and local vehicle taxes, display **“varies locally”** and link the official lookup/rate table rather than calculating an unsupported statewide rate.
- “None” means no tax of that type at that government level; it does not mean the underlying transaction or income is free of all federal, state, and local taxes.
- Gross-receipts taxes (Delaware), Arizona TPT, Hawaii GET, registration/document fees, and vehicle value taxes are legally distinct from ordinary retail sales tax; retain those labels in the UI.
